t: Look up at the long stone frieze, Commerce Welcoming All Nations. It was carved for the façade of the Hall of Commerce, which opened in 1842 in the City of London. The relief is Portland stone, about 22 metres long. It's by Musgrave Watson, an English sculptor who lived from 1804 to 1847 and is best known for the bas-relief at the base of Nelson's Column. This frieze is regarded as his principal surviving architectural sculpture, and it established his reputation as an independent sculptor.
